clue.text: Glazed look of chap with elbow dislocated

indicators.note: a dislocated joint is knocked out of place, so these letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A man with a dislocated elbow wears a dazed, glassy expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glazed look' suggests a vacant stare, but it is a ceramic finish; 'dislocated' rearranges CHAP and ELBOW together.
explanation.definitionFit: Peachblow is a pinkish porcelain glaze, the look of a fired surface.

clue.text: A horse below standard indicates overriding.

indicators.note: in a down answer, the horse piece sits below the standard piece

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a mount is a horse for riding, with A kept

explanation.surface: A substandard horse signals that something has been overruled.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme, taking precedence over all else.

clue.text: Cold in Harley Street?

parts.note: Harley Street is London's street of private doctors, so this asks for the medical word for chilly, not a sniffle there

explanation.surface: Someone catches a chill in London's medical district.
explanation.walkthrough: Harley Street in London is famous for private medical practices.
explanation.definitionFit: Algid is a medical term for cold or chilly, used of fevers and patients.

clue.text: The sort of spectacles that last a fortnight

definitions.text: The sort of spectacles that last a fortnight

parts.words: The sort of spectacles that last a fortnight
parts.note: spectacles suggest eyeglasses with half-lenses, but also sights in the sky; a lunar phase covering half a month lasts about two weeks

explanation.surface: Glasses that wear out after two weeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-moon glasses have half-lenses, and half a lunar month is roughly two weeks.

clue.text: For him the drums are playing their part

definitions.text: For him the drums are playing their part

parts.words: For him the drums are playing their part
parts.note: drums suggests a band, but eardrums do their job for someone hearing

explanation.surface: A musician hears the drum section performing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hearing relies on eardrums, which vibrate as sound arrives.

clue.text: Cheerless outcome of a victory effort

parts.note: a win is a victory
a try is an attempt or effort

explanation.surface: A gloomy result from a bid to win.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintry weather is bleak, and a wintry smile is cold and joyless.

clue.text: Key to clever film star

parts.note: G is a musical key
able means clever or capable

explanation.surface: A tip for a smart movie actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Clark Gable was a Hollywood leading man.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark Gable was a famous Hollywood actor of the 1930s and 1940s.

clue.text: First two characters in Genesis with little sign of heavenly influence

parts.note: the opening two letters of the word Genesis
mini means little

explanation.surface: The start of the Bible with a small heavenly sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' is a zodiac sign; astrology claims the stars influence us.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini is a sign of the zodiac, the Twins, said by astrologers to shape character.

clue.text: Sort of vision of Lion and Crab moving round universe

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round, surrounding, the universe piece
moving means the letters of lion and crab are shifted into a new order

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for universal or universe, as in film certificates

explanation.surface: Two zodiac creatures circling the cosmos, a sort of vision.
explanation.walkthrough: The zodiac creatures are fodder, not star signs. 'moving' gives BINOCLAR, which 'round' wraps about U.
explanation.definitionFit: Binocular vision uses both eyes together, giving depth perception.

clue.text: She's the topless beauty of the north

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its first letter, its top in a down answer

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A northern beauty who goes bare-chested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is the definition: a girl's name. 'Topless' removes the first letter of BELLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a woman's first name, so it can stand for she.

clue.text: One star Roman general

explanation.surface: A single star awarded to a Roman commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Regulus is the brightest star in Leo, and Marcus Atilius Regulus was a Roman commander in the First Punic War.

clue.text: Virtually nothing in a name

explanation.surface: There is hardly anything in what something is called.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominal fee is a token, tiny sum; nominal also means existing in title only, by naming.

clue.text: Form of address when married to a gardener

parts.note: Adam, tending Eden, was the first gardener

explanation.surface: How one addresses a woman who has wed a gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam is the crossword's stock gardener, from his work in the Garden of Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a polite way of speaking to a woman, a courteous term of address.

clue.text: Peace proposal giving Ireland northern representation

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
an icon is an image or representation

explanation.surface: A peace plan that would give Northern Ireland a voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ireland northern' looks like Northern Ireland, but the two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An eirenicon is a proposal made to promote peace or reconciliation, from Greek for peaceful.

clue.text: An elder could be so removed

definitions.text: An elder could be so removed

parts.words: An elder could be so removed
parts.note: reads like a senior being ousted from office, but an elder is a tree that can be pulled out of the ground, roots and all

explanation.surface: A church elder might be ousted this way.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a shrub, and a shrub pulled out roots and all has been dug out of the soil entirely.

clue.text: Times of pecuniary need likely from July 15th

explanation.surface: Hard-up times expected from mid-July.
explanation.walkthrough: July 15th is St Swithin's Day: British folklore says rain that day brings forty days of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Saving for a hard-up time is putting by for later; folklore says St Swithin's rain lasts forty days.

clue.text: Run when the predator returns

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so the word for the predator is read backwards

parts.note: a wolf is a predator

explanation.surface: Flee when the hunting animal comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: To flow is to run, as a river or tap runs with water.

clue.text: Micro-organisms in bismuth a trace unusual

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters appear in an unusual order

parts.note: Bi is the chemical symbol for bismuth

explanation.surface: Germs found in a strange trace of a metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteria are single-celled microbes, the commonest germs.

clue.text: Miss Spenlow incompetent but pleasing

annotationWithheld.why: Miss Spenlow incompetent but pleasing (8) for ADORABLE: DORA in ABLE needs 'incompetent' read as 'in' plus 'competent', one printed word doing two jobs

clue.text: Observe a small shoot

explanation.surface: Notice a little sprout.
explanation.definitionFit: Twig is slang for notice or grasp, and a twig is a slender shoot of a branch.

clue.text: The song of the gypsy

parts.note: a roving traveller would sing of a life on the road

explanation.surface: The tune a Romany traveller sings.
explanation.definitionFit: A gypsy is a roamer, and Schubert's song of the roaming life bears this title.

clue.text: Humour when duty leaves room for it

indicators.note: making room for something means opening a space to hold it, so it goes inside

parts.note: a levy is a tax or duty

explanation.surface: Being lighthearted when your obligations allow.
explanation.definitionFit: Levity is lightheartedness, a frivolous humour.

clue.text: Old king — say the diminutive Albert?

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means
Bert is a short form of the name Albert

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch, maybe a little Albert?
explanation.walkthrough: Egbert was a ninth-century king of Wessex.
explanation.definitionFit: Egbert was an early English king of Wessex.

clue.text: Pressure on an astute fighter

indicators.note: one piece on another means it follows it, so pressure comes after astute

parts.note: fly is slang for astute or knowing
weight is pressure, as in the weight of responsibility

explanation.surface: Putting pressure on a clever boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: Flyweight is the lightest boxing class, so a fighter at that weight is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A flyweight is a boxer in the lightest weight division.

clue.text: He had lots of dips in Dickensian London

definitions.text: He had lots of dips in Dickensian London

parts.words: He had lots of dips in Dickensian London
parts.note: dips suggests swims, but a dip is a pickpocket; Oliver Twist's gang leader ran many

explanation.surface: A man who swam often in Victorian London.
explanation.definitionFit: In Oliver Twist, the villain trains a gang of young pickpockets.

clue.text: Somewhat curtailed but blooming early

indicators.note: curtailed means its tail is cut, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: rather means somewhat, as in rather cold

explanation.surface: A flower that is cut short but still flowers early.
explanation.walkthrough: Rathe is an old word, used of flowers that bloom early in the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Rathe is an archaic adjective for early, especially of blossoms appearing before others.

clue.text: Woven fabric — tip-top choice

parts.note: something tip-top suits to a T, so T stands for perfect
will is free choice, as in of your own will

explanation.surface: A first-rate selection of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip-top' looks like praise of the choice, but it gives T, as in 'to a T'.
explanation.definitionFit: Twill is cloth woven with diagonal ridges, like denim.

clue.text: Gang ran items abroad, including the hard stuff

indicators.note: the words before including contain the answer within them, spanning three of them

explanation.surface: Smugglers ship goods overseas, among them strong liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The hard stuff' suggests spirits, but it means a hard rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a very hard igneous rock, used for building and kerbs.

clue.text: In true Liberal fashion, put up again

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape it anew, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: In the style of a genuine Liberal, constructed once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rebuilt has been constructed a second time, raised anew after falling or being demolished.

clue.text: One's moved by end of play — wanting to know more?

indicators.note: moved means the letters of ones are shifted into a new order

parts.note: read as the plural ones, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here of play

explanation.surface: A theatregoer is touched by the play's finale and keen to learn more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's moved' reads as being emotionally touched, but ONES is rearranged to NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosey person is inquisitive, prying into others' affairs.

clue.text: An agent, proverbially broad-minded

explanation.surface: A sales representative, said to have an open mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial traveller is a sales agent, and the proverb says travel broadens the mind.
